name: Healthy Streets in Shanghai's Inner City (9 Health Statements)
description:
Method replication: same task, scale and design as the paper; the images are not the paper's stimuli (91 Baidu street views re-fetched inside Shanghai's Inner Ring Road, 2018 or later, front views along the road as in the paper's Baidu images).

Original study: Shao, Yin & Ma (2024), Land 13(1), 48. About 609,000 Baidu street views of Shanghai's inner city were grouped into nine streetscape types by their visual composition. One typical image of each type was shown online (via WeChat) to people who had lived in the inner city for over 12 months, who rated the 9 statements in this template from 1 (completely disagree) to 5 (completely agree): three each on physical, mental and social health opportunities. Type means were mapped across the city to assess health equity.

Differences from the original study: (1) Each participant sees 9 street views drawn at random from 91 new images, instead of the same nine typical images, one per streetscape type; the clustering into types is not part of the template. (2) The paper gave elevated roads a fixed lowest score; here no elevated-road images are rated by rule. (3) The paper's verification questionnaire is not included. (4) Gender and age are our additions; the 12-month residence question is asked instead of used to screen people out.
author: Shao, Yin & Ma
